verdicts.why: Reads the un- negation as flat steadfastness and separates it from undaunted's faced-down fear; positive charge fits a purpose that held.
Names the illegal payment as an outright accusation against buy's understatement; squarely on the gloss.
The contempt-by-implication reading fits the corrupt-payment gloss, and both examples are the bought-official sense.
Treats the thing as vice itself, which is what 'having the nature of vice' says; the contrast with wicked stays inside the word.
Formal register label plus the extreme-and-criminal verdict matches the gloss; the example fits.
A casting term that marks the villain's role without condemning; neutral charge is right for this theatre sense and the Iago example fits.
Wickedness pitched into the criminal, delivered as a sentence — that is the gloss's force; 'public' reads as the word's sound, not a usage claim.
Weighs the sin as an enormity against sinful's plain logging; fits the iniquity gloss and the example.
Reads reform as recovery denied, which is exactly 'insusceptible of reform' through this word's picture.
Withheld redemption as a final verdict fits the gloss and correctly ranks it against its three synset-mates.
Abstract condemnation of the wickedness versus villainous's aim at the doer stays inside the word; 'nefarious schemes' fits.
Liability to sin, not sin committed, is the gloss; the mild negative charge is plausible and the example fits.
Plain wickedness-as-sin without iniquitous's swell fits the gloss; the lipstick example is this sense.
Reads the wickedness as distance from godliness — a word-internal picture consistent with 'wicked because believed to be a sin'.
Same refusal of reform, distinguished from irredeemable only by the plainer prefix; on the gloss.
The flat statement that reform will not take is the gloss verbatim; the contrast with irredeemable stays in the word.
Vice as settled bent fits 'having the nature of vice' and correctly avoids the savage/violent sense.
Extreme wickedness cast as a villain's character fits the gloss; both examples carry the wickedness back to a doer.
The unhedged moral verdict covering both principle and practice tracks the gloss exactly.
Deceit with a victim who is out something is the gloss's 'deprive by deceit'; charge fits.
Informal register label and the small-mean sting describe the word's force on the same deprive-by-deceit gloss.
Flat accusation of bad faith with no gain stated fits 'be false to; be dishonest with'; the example is this sense.
Falseness aimed at the other's mind is a word-internal distinction from deceive on the same gloss.
Caring about nothing weighed as a fault fits the trait gloss and justifies the negative charge.
Settled disposition stated without apathy's reproach fits the gloss; negative is still plausible for a lack, and the example is 'things generally'.
Inactivity traced to drained energy, read as suffered, is the gloss's 'resulting from lethargy' through the word.
Missing interest as feeling gone dull fits the figurative trait gloss and correctly softens the blame against apathy.
Staying inactive and starting nothing with no claim about feeling is the gloss's 'remaining inactive; lack of initiative'.
